## Load Required Libraries

```{r load-libraries, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(rpart)
library(rpart.plot)
library(ROCR)
library(caret)
library(ranger)
```

## Problem Set

### Question 1 (2 points)

Read in the heart_train.csv data as a data-frame. Conduct a quick summary inspection of your data.

```{r read-data}
heart_train <- read.csv("heart_train.csv")

# Summary inspection
str(heart_train)
summary(heart_train)
sum(is.na(heart_train))
```


### Question 2 (2 points)

Analyze the prevalence of heart disease in the dataset.

```{r heart-disease-prevalence}
heart_disease_count <- sum(heart_train$target == 1)
total_count <- nrow(heart_train)
heart_disease_percentage <- (heart_disease_count / total_count) * 100

print(paste("Number of people with heart disease:", heart_disease_count))
print(paste("Percentage of people with heart disease:", round(heart_disease_percentage, 2), "%"))
```


### Question 3 (2 points)

Convert the target attribute to a factor.

```{r convert-target}
heart_train$target <- factor(heart_train$target, levels = c(1, 0), labels = c("Yes", "No"))
```


### Question 4 (8 points)

Build and prune an rpart decision tree.

```{r decision-tree}
set.seed(2)

# Build the tree
tree_model <- rpart(target ~ ., data = heart_train, method = "class")

# Find the optimal cp
optimal_cp <- tree_model$cptable[which.min(tree_model$cptable[,"xerror"]),"CP"]

# Prune the tree
pruned_tree <- prune(tree_model, cp = optimal_cp)

# Plot the pruned tree
rpart.plot(pruned_tree, extra = 1, under = TRUE, cex = 0.8)
```


### Question 5 (2 points)
considering the parameters there would be no changes required in the controls.

### Question 7 (10 points)

Predict on the test set and create a confusion matrix.

```{r test-predictions}
# Read and prepare test data
heart_test <- read.csv("heart_test.csv")
heart_test$target <- factor(heart_test$target, levels = c(1, 0), labels = c("Yes", "No"))

# Predict on test data
predictions <- predict(pruned_tree, heart_test, type = "class")

# Create confusion matrix
conf_matrix <- table(Predicted = predictions, Actual = heart_test$target)
print(conf_matrix)

# Calculate accuracy
accuracy <- sum(diag(conf_matrix)) / sum(conf_matrix)
print(paste("Accuracy:", round(accuracy, 4)))
```


### Question 8 (2 points)

Analyze False Positives vs False Negatives.

```{r false-positives-negatives}
false_positives <- conf_matrix["Yes", "No"]
false_negatives <- conf_matrix["No", "Yes"]

print(paste("False Positives:", false_positives))
print(paste("False Negatives:", false_negatives))
```


### Question 9 (8 points)

Create an ROC curve.

```{r roc-curve}
# Get probabilities
probs <- predict(pruned_tree, heart_test, type = "prob")[,"Yes"]

# Create prediction object
pred <- prediction(probs, heart_test$target)

# Create performance object
perf <- performance(pred, "tpr", "fpr")

# Create data frame for ggplot
roc_data <- data.frame(FPR = perf@x.values[[1]], TPR = perf@y.values[[1]])

# Plot ROC curve
ggplot(roc_data, aes(x = FPR, y = TPR)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(title = "ROC Curve for Heart Disease Prediction",
       x = "False Positive Rate", 
       y = "True Positive Rate") +
  theme_minimal()
```


### Question 10 (2 points)

Find the AUC of your ROC curve.

```{r auc}
auc <- performance(pred, "auc")@y.values[[1]]
print(paste("AUC:", round(auc, 4)))
```


### Question 11 (5 points)

Plot Accuracy vs Cutoff.

```{r accuracy-vs-cutoff}
acc <- performance(pred, "acc")
acc_data <- data.frame(Cutoff = acc@x.values[[1]], Accuracy = acc@y.values[[1]])

ggplot(acc_data, aes(x = Cutoff, y = Accuracy)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(title = "Accuracy vs Cutoff",
       x = "Cutoff", 
       y = "Accuracy") +
  theme_minimal()
```


### Question 12 (15 points)

Tune a random forest model using the caret package.

```{r random-forest}
set.seed(2)

# Define hyperparameters
hyper_grid <- expand.grid(
  mtry = c(2, 4, 6),
  splitrule = "gini",
  min.node.size = c(1, 3, 5)
)

# Define training control
ctrl <- trainControl(
  method = "cv",
  number = 10,
  classProbs = TRUE,
  summaryFunction = twoClassSummary
)

# Train the model
rf_model <- train(
  target ~ .,
  data = heart_train,
  method = "ranger",
  num.trees = 500,
  importance = "impurity",
  tuneGrid = hyper_grid,
  trControl = ctrl,
  metric = "ROC"
)

# Print best model
print(rf_model$bestTune)

# Predict on test set
rf_predictions <- predict(rf_model, heart_test)
rf_probs <- predict(rf_model, heart_test, type = "prob")

# Create confusion matrix
rf_conf_matrix <- confusionMatrix(rf_predictions, heart_test$target)
print(rf_conf_matrix)
```


### Bonus Question (2 points)

Compare the accuracy of your tuned Random Forest model to your pruned Decision Tree on the test sample.

```{r compare-accuracies}
dt_accuracy <- accuracy  # from Question 7
rf_accuracy <- rf_conf_matrix$overall["Accuracy"]

print(paste("Decision Tree Accuracy:", round(dt_accuracy, 4)))
print(paste("Random Forest Accuracy:", round(rf_accuracy, 4)))
```
